To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a semiautomated segmentation algorithm based on EPI images has been developed and optimized for cervical spine, and that the performance of this algorithm depends on the degree of geometric distortion of the EPI images.

we developed and validated a semiautomated algorithm for the segmentation of human SC based on EPI data, and that the accuracy of this algorithm was significantly affected by image geometric distortion.

a tailored semiautomated method for segmenting EPI of human spine is able to identify with a high level of accuracy the spinal canal and SC and that geometric distortion of EPI is an important factor to be taken into account when developing a processing pipeline for SC fMRI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a semiautomated segmentation method for SC EPI, which is able to identify both the SC and the spinal canal.
a semiautomatic approach to SC segmentation that exploits both the spatial and temporal information of the EPI.
the development of a semiautomated method for segmenting EPI images of human spine, based on the use of both spatial and temporal information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method presented here is a valid alternative to manual segmentation and can be applied to a wide range of SC EPI data.
our method is able to segment the SC from cervical spine EPI images with high accuracy, but the performance of the method is affected by geometric distortions.

the proposed method represents a significant improvement over the state of the art in SC segmentation and that the method's performance is limited by the presence of geometric distortions in the EPI series, which can be reduced by increasing the strength of the main magnetic field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method provides a robust, semiautomated approach for segmenting EPI images of the human spine and is likely to facilitate future SC fMRI investigations.

the proposed semiautomatic algorithm is able to accurately and reproducibly segment the SC in EPI series acquired with a standard cervical spine imaging protocol, with the added advantage of being able to identify the SC in Epi images of the entire spine, not only the cervical region.
the proposed semiautomated method is able to identify with a high accuracy the SC and spinal canal in EPI series of the cervical spine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method is a promising candidate for the development of a fully automatic processing pipeline for human SC fMRI.
the use of temporal information in segmentation algorithms for EPI images of the SC can improve their performance.
temporal features can significantly improve the performance of SC segmentation algorithms, but their use may be compromised in the presence of significant image distortion.
